London generates roughly a quarter of the UK’s economic output
With the official London unemployment rate having hit 7.4% in March 2026, this suggests that weaker demand in the labour market is the key contributor recently to involuntary worklessness in London.
The most recent ONS data release showed London’s real GVA grew by only 0.3% in 2023 (compared to 0.4% for the UK as a whole). Estimates by GLA Economics suggest a modest strengthening of economic growth in London over the last two years, with real GVA expected to have risen by 1.1% in 2024 and 1.9% in 2025.
